20261103CA84431.description: California Proposition 1. Authorizes $11.25 billion of bonds for affordable housing, including for veterans.
20261103CA84431.summary: This ballot measure would authorize $11.25 billion of state bonds to finance affordable housing programs, with $1.25 billion of that amount set aside for housing for veterans.

20261103CA84432.description: California Proposition 2. Raises the maximum amount of money in the state's rainy day fund.
20261103CA84432.summary: This proposed amendment to California's constitution would raise the cap on how much money can be set aside in the state's Budget Stabilization Account from 10% to 20% of estimated general fund revenues.

20261103CA84433.description: California Proposition 3. Makes higher income tax rates permanent.
20261103CA84433.summary: This proposed amendment to California's constitution would repeal the December 2031 expiration date for higher income tax rates charged to those in the state's upper income tax brackets.
20261103CA84433.seatName: 3 - Permanently extend high-income tax for school funding

20261103CA84434.description: California Proposition 4. Repeals a ban on public funding of campaigns.
20261103CA84434.summary: This ballot measure would repeal a ban on public funding of campaigns and instead allow programs that provide public financing to candidates.
20261103CA84434.seatName: 4 - Repeal ban on public campaign finance

20261103CA84435.description: California Proposition 5. Changes the process for recalling and replacing elected officials.
20261103CA84435.summary: This proposed amendment to California's constitution would change the way replacements are selected when someone is recalled from office by voters. Vacancies would be filled by succession, appointment or special election rather than by electing a new official simultaneously with the recall vote.
20261103CA84435.seatName: 5 - Require separate election for recalled officials

20261103CA84436.description: California Proposition 37. Authorizes $25 billion of bonds for loans to middle-income buyers of new homes.
20261103CA84436.summary: This ballot measure would authorize $25 billion of state bonds to finance loans to purchasers of new homes whose family income is no more than twice the median for the area.

20261103CA84437.description: California Proposition 38. Authorizes $8.4 billion of bonds for immunotherapy research for cancer and other diseases.
20261103CA84437.summary: This ballot measure would authorize $8.4 billion of bonds for immunotherapy research for cancer, heart disease, Alzheimer's disease and other ailments.

20261103CA84438.description: California Proposition 39. Requires government-issued identification to vote.
20261103CA84438.summary: This proposed amendment to California's constitution would require voters to provide government-issued identification to cast a ballot in person or the last four digits of a government-issued identification number to cast a mail-in ballot.

20261103CA84439.description: California Proposition 40. Imposes a 5% tax on those whose wealth is over $1 billion.
20261103CA84439.summary: This proposed amendment to California's constitution would impose a one-time 5% tax on individuals and trusts with wealth over $1 billion, with revenue to go toward healthcare, food assistance and education. Revenue from the tax would be exempt from state spending limits.
20261103CA84439.seatName: 40 - Impose one-time wealth tax over $1 billion

20261103CA84440.description: California Proposition 41. Requires audits of tax programs and subjects new taxes to spending limits.
20261103CA84440.summary: This proposed amendment to California's constitution would require preelection audits for initiatives proposing special taxes and additional audits every four years. It also would prohibit new tax revenue from being exempted from state spending limits.
20261103CA84440.seatName: 41 - Require audit of programs funded by special taxes

20261103CA84441.description: California Proposition 42. Prohibits taxes on personal savings, assets and retirement holdings.
20261103CA84441.summary: This proposed amendment to California's constitution would prohibit taxes on personal savings, assets and retirement holdings.
20261103CA84441.seatName: 42 - Prohibit new state taxes on personal property

20261103CA84442.description: California Proposition 43. Requires a two-thirds vote to pass citizen-initiated local taxes.
20261103CA84442.summary: This proposed amendment to California's constitution would require a two-thirds vote to approve local special taxes proposed by citizen initiative and would prohibit local property taxes beyond what is already allowed under the state constitution.
20261103CA84442.seatName: 43 - Raise approval threshold for voter-initiated special taxes

20261103CA84443.description: California Proposition 44. Limits administrative expenses for certain nonprofit healthcare centers.
20261103CA84443.summary: This ballot measure would require nonprofit federally qualified healthcare centers to spend at least 90% of their revenue on mission-related activities and allow penalties for those with higher administrative costs.

20261103CA84444.description: California Proposition 45. Shortens deadlines for environmental reviews and government permits.
20261103CA84444.summary: This ballot measure would shorten deadlines for environmental reviews and government permits for certain projects involving housing, clean energy, water, public health or safety, internet access, education facilities and transportation.
20261103CA84444.seatName: 45 - Modify environmental review to expedite projects

20261103CA85061.description: Fresno Measure S. Imposes a half-cent sales tax for public safety, streets and city services.
20261103CA85061.summary: This ballot measure would establish a half-cent sales tax in Fresno, raising about $65 million annually for 10 years or until a county transportation tax is adopted, to fund streets, police and fire staffing, emergency response, transit, airport improvements and other services.
20261103CA85061.seatName: Fresno-S - Public safety, infrastructure restoration, and city general services sales tax

20261103CA85062.description: Los Angeles Measure TE. Exempts Palisades fire victims from a tax on property sales over $5 million.
20261103CA85062.summary: This ballot measure would exempt sales of residential properties damaged or destroyed by the Palisades fire from Los Angeles' Proposition ULA tax on properties over $5 million. The exemption or refund would apply to sales by the original owner between January 2025 and January 2030.
20261103CA85062.seatName: Los Angeles-TE - One-time property transfer tax exemption for victims of the January 2025 fire disaster

20261103CA85063.description: Los Angeles Measure LA. Creates a two-year budget cycle and a capital infrastructure plan.
20261103CA85063.summary: This ballot measure would establish a two-year budget cycle and a capital infrastructure plan for Los Angeles, expand the public works director's authority and exempt certain critical infrastructure projects from competitive bidding rules.
20261103CA85063.seatName: Los Angeles-LA - Establish a capital infrastructure plan and a two-year city budget cycle

20261103CA85064.description: Los Angeles Measure PL. Replaces area planning commissions with a single appeals commission.
20261103CA85064.summary: This ballot measure would replace Los Angeles' seven area planning commissions with a single Neighborhood Appeals Commission to hear land-use appeals and would make other changes to the city's planning and land-use approval process.
20261103CA85064.seatName: Los Angeles-PL - Establish a Neighborhood Appeals Commission

20261103CA85065.description: Los Angeles Measure EE. Changes city ethics, campaign finance and governance rules.
20261103CA85065.summary: This ballot measure would make several changes to Los Angeles' ethics and governance rules, including increasing campaign finance penalties, raising the signature requirement for referendum petitions and strengthening the independence of police and fire department watchdogs.
20261103CA85065.seatName: Los Angeles-EE - City ethics, elections, and governance

20261103CA85066.description: Los Angeles Measure PRK. Doubles the minimum share of the city budget for parks and recreation.
20261103CA85066.summary: This ballot measure would double the minimum share of Los Angeles' general fund dedicated to the Department of Recreation and Parks, phased in over 10 years, without creating a new tax.
20261103CA85066.seatName: Los Angeles-PRK - Increase the minimum budget allocated to the Department of Recreation and Parks

20261103CA85067.description: Los Angeles Measure PRT. Changes lease and governance rules for airport, harbor and utility departments.
20261103CA85067.summary: This ballot measure would allow the Los Angeles City Council to authorize leases of up to 66 years for the airports and water and power departments, require some airport commissioners to live near Los Angeles International and Van Nuys airports and require the Harbor Department to fund waterfront public access projects.
20261103CA85067.seatName: Los Angeles-PRT - Airports, harbor, water and power departments

20261103CA85068.description: Los Angeles Measure SC. Applies city campaign finance rules to school board candidates.
20261103CA85068.summary: This ballot measure would apply the same campaign finance rules to Los Angeles Board of Education candidates that apply to mayoral candidates, with certain exceptions, and allow the City Council to make further changes by ordinance.
20261103CA85068.seatName: Los Angeles-SC - Allow changes by ordinance for Board of Education campaign finance rules

20261103CA85069.description: Los Angeles Measure FD. Imposes a half-cent sales tax to fund the fire department.
20261103CA85069.summary: This citizen-initiated ballot measure would establish a half-cent sales tax in Los Angeles to fund the fire department, including staffing, vehicles, equipment, wildfire preparedness and fire station construction and maintenance.
20261103CA85069.seatName: Los Angeles-FD - Sales tax for fire department funding

20261103CA85070.description: Oakland Measure EE. Makes the mayor the city's chief executive with veto power.
20261103CA85070.summary: This proposed amendment to Oakland's charter would make the mayor the city's chief executive with veto power, allow the City Council to override vetoes and confirm certain appointments, require City Council members to work full time and have the Public Ethics Commission set salaries for elected officials.
20261103CA85070.seatName: Oakland-EE - Mayor-council government and mayoral powers

20261103CA85071.description: Oakland Measure FF. Eliminates most foreclosure exemptions from the property transfer tax.
20261103CA85071.summary: This ballot measure would eliminate most foreclosure exemptions from Oakland's real property transfer tax, raising an estimated $4 million to $13 million annually beginning in 2027.

20261103CA85072.description: San Francisco Proposition A. Merges, renames or eliminates various city boards and commissions.
20261103CA85072.summary: This proposed amendment to San Francisco's charter would make broad cleanup changes to the city's boards, commissions and departments, including eliminating, merging or renaming several advisory bodies, moving others from the charter into city code and removing obsolete language. It also would expand the city administrator's authority over real estate and allow the Board of Supervisors to rename city departments and agencies by ordinance.
20261103CA85072.seatName: San Francisco-A - Department, board, commission, and advisory body updates charter amendment

20261103CA85073.description: San Francisco Proposition B. Authorizes creation of a municipal finance corporation and a public bank.
20261103CA85073.summary: This proposed amendment to San Francisco's charter would authorize the creation of a municipal finance corporation and a public bank as nonprofit corporations, if adequate funding is available, each with its own oversight commission and board of directors.
20261103CA85073.seatName: San Francisco-B - Municipal finance corporation and public bank charter amendment

20261103CA85074.description: San Francisco Proposition C. Increases required annual funding for the Housing Trust Fund.
20261103CA85074.summary: This proposed amendment to San Francisco's charter would increase required annual funding for the Housing Trust Fund beginning in fiscal year 2028-29 until it reaches $125 million, expand the fund's allowable uses and extend it to 2058.
20261103CA85074.seatName: San Francisco-C - San Francisco housing trust fund charter amendment

20261103CA85075.description: San Francisco Proposition D. Limits how measures are placed on the ballot and raises signature requirements.
20261103CA85075.summary: This proposed amendment to San Francisco's charter would end the ability of the mayor or four supervisors to place measures on the ballot without a vote of the full Board of Supervisors and increase the number of voter signatures required to qualify citizen initiatives.
20261103CA85075.seatName: San Francisco-D - Changes to ballot measure process charter amendment

20261103CA85076.description: San Francisco Proposition E. Expands the city administrator's contracting authority and extends the term to 10 years.
20261103CA85076.summary: This proposed amendment to San Francisco's charter would give the city administrator authority over most city contracting rules and technology policy, raise the dollar thresholds requiring Board of Supervisors approval of contracts and extend the city administrator's term from five years to 10.
20261103CA85076.seatName: San Francisco-E - Extending the City Administrator's duties and changes to city contracting charter amendment

20261103CA85077.description: San Francisco Proposition F. Allows the mayor to reorganize departments and hire and fire department heads.
20261103CA85077.summary: This proposed amendment to San Francisco's charter would allow the mayor to reorganize most executive branch departments, hire deputy mayors and hire and fire most department heads without board or commission involvement.
20261103CA85077.seatName: San Francisco-F - Changes to executive branch management charter amendment

20261103CA85078.description: San Francisco Proposition G. Reopens the Upper Great Highway to private vehicles on weekdays.
20261103CA85078.summary: This ballot measure would reopen the Upper Great Highway in San Francisco's Sunset Dunes Park to private vehicles on weekdays, while keeping it closed to private traffic from Friday evening through early Monday and on holidays.
20261103CA85078.seatName: San Francisco-G - Allowing private vehicles on the Great Highway in Sunset Dunes Park

20261103CA85079.description: San Francisco Proposition H. Imposes a parcel tax to fund public transit operations.
20261103CA85079.summary: This ballot measure would impose an annual parcel tax in San Francisco from 2027 through 2042, based on a property's type and building size, to fund public transit operations. Most homeowners 65 and older would be exempt or receive a reduction.
20261103CA85079.seatName: San Francisco-H - Parcel tax to fund public transit operations

20261103CA85080.description: San Francisco Proposition I. Restructures the transfer tax on property sales of $10 million or more to fund housing.
20261103CA85080.summary: This ballot measure would cut San Francisco's existing transfer tax on property sales of $10 million or more in half and replace it with a new tax of about the same amount, with revenue dedicated to affordable housing and tenant protection programs.
20261103CA85080.seatName: San Francisco-I - Changes to real property transfer tax

20261103CA85081.description: San Francisco Proposition J. Eliminates the transfer tax exemption for most foreclosed properties.
20261103CA85081.summary: This ballot measure would eliminate San Francisco's partial transfer tax exemption for foreclosures on most properties, other than single-family homes and small residential and mixed-use buildings, beginning March 1, 2027.
20261103CA85081.seatName: San Francisco-J - Eliminate real property transfer tax foreclosure exemption
